data.title: Commonwealth Heads of Government 2026 statement between the UK and Australia
data.author: PMC
data.summary: Addressing online violence in our democracies – promoting equality in Commonwealth Parliaments.A toxic online environment is a threat to all Commonwealth democracies. It threatens our values and undermines our people’s freedom and choices. Workplace violence in any context is unacceptable, including that faced by journalists and media who are crucial to protecting freedom and democracy. We also condemn rising violence and aggression towards all frontline workers, including health and retail workers.

data.title: 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting
data.author: PMC
data.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will travel to Antigua and Barbuda to attend the 2026 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) from 31 October to 4 November 2026.Representatives from over 50 countries are expected to attend the meeting to discuss shared challenges and opportunities under the theme of Accelerating Partnerships and Investment for a Prosperous Commonwealth.The Commonwealth is a unique and diverse grouping of 56 countries, representing 2.7 billion people from both advanced and developing economies across the world.

data.title: Press conference - Canberra
data.author: PMC
data.summary: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good morning. This has been a big week in parliament. Yesterday, the House of Representatives passed the Digital Duty of Care legislation. It is vital that this get the support of the Senate. It does two things essentially, the first is it makes big tech accountable. Just as the media organisations represented here are accountable for what’s on their platforms, they should be held to account for the role that they play and what appears on their platforms and which therefore then get circulated right around Australia.

data.title: Digital duty of care
data.author: PMC
data.summary: Well, thanks very much, Mr. Speaker.For several years now, Australians have been increasingly concerned about the impact of the online world on the welfare of children and on the cohesiveness of our society.A movement for change, begun and led by brave parents who saw their children's lives taken by cruel and highly addictive social media, created a remarkable period of bipartisanship that put Australia in the forefront of global movements to bring about online safety.

data.title: Western Sydney goes international
data.author: PMC
data.summary: The first international arrival to Australia’s newest full-service airport has touched down, with Air New Zealand NZ165 from Auckland landing at Western Sydney International (Nancy-Bird Walton) Airport earlier this morning.After a short stopover, a full flight was boarded for the return leg and NZ166 departed. This is the first of three weekly return flights between Western Sydney International Airport (WSI) and New Zealand’s largest city.

data.summary: As the House meets for the first time since the horrific events of last Monday, it is appropriate that our very first act is to speak about the Member for Indi, Dr Helen Haines.Her husband, Phil Haines, is with us this morning. data.title: Press conference - Sydney
data.author: PMC
data.summary: ANTHONY ALBANESE, PRIME MINISTER: Good evening. Tonight, I want to update Australians on a serious incident that has occurred in Victoria. This afternoon, Helen Haines, the Member for Indi, was attacked outside her electorate office in Wangaratta. All of our thoughts are with Helen, her family, her friends, her team, and her community at this extremely difficult time. We are praying for her full recovery. I want to thank the first responders for their extraordinary work. There is a major police investigation underway, and I can confirm that a suspect is in custody.

data.title: Centenary of parliament sitting
data.author: PMC
data.summary: To mark 100 years since our national parliament first met in Canberra, the 48th Australian Parliament will sit for a day at Old Parliament House in April next year.The special sitting day will see Question Time, legislation and other statements return to the Chambers of Old Parliament House for the first time in decades.In 1927, the “Provisional Parliament” was opened in Canberra and our national parliamentarians continued to meet in that building until 1988.Learning from our democratic history and institutions is more important than ever.

data.title: Departmental ministerial appointment
data.author: PMC
data.summary: The Governor-General has accepted my recommendation to appoint Senator the Hon Tim Ayres, Minister for Industry and Innovation and Minister for Science, to administer the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (PM&C).This appointment reflects Minister Ayres’ role contributing to oversight of the Office of Artificial Intelligence, which is designing world-leading national AI standards to ensure Australians can share the benefits of this transformative technology, safely, and that AI works in Australia’s interests.

data.title: First update on the Defence Estate Audit
data.author: PMC
data.summary: The Albanese Government is acting on the independent Defence Estate Audit, and progressing the most significant reform to Australia’s Defence estate in our nation’s history.Keeping Australians safe is the Government’s priority, and as part of that we must ensure the Australian Defence Force (ADF) has access to facilities that are fit for purpose.In response to the independent Audit, the Government agreed to divest or partially divest 67 sites that were underutilised by Defence, not fit-for-purpose, and costly for Defence to maintain.

https://www.pm.gov.au/node/47724.label: First update on the Defence Estate Audit
